Hello and welcome :)

I am a developmental scientist with a background in economics. I study how family economic circumstances shape children's development and young adults' life chances.

My research sits at the intersection of developmental science,
economics, and policy. I completed my Ph.D. in Developmental
Psychology at the University of Pittsburgh, where my dissertation
followed more than 7,000 young adults over 24 years to examine how
the composition and timing of childhood family wealth relate to
outcomes across education, economic wellbeing, mental health, and
family formation.

I bring an unusual path to this work: before turning to developmental
science, I earned a doctorate in economics and spent a decade as a
professor and policy researcher in Ukraine, advising national health
and social reform efforts in partnership with the World Bank, WHO,
and the World Economic Forum.

As an educator with fifteen years of university teaching across two
countries, I teach developmental psychology, research methods, and
quantitative analysis — helping students connect developmental
science to the real economic and social conditions of children's
lives.
